description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/README.md is stale on three live API surfaces. Anyone reading the README to learn the CalendarsBackend trait gets the wrong signatures.

1. README §'CalendarsBackend trait' lines 115-121 — update_per_user_properties documented with
       patch: serde_json::Value
   actual (backend.rs:148-158): patch: PatchObject.
   The Value type would not even compile against today's handler call site.

2. README lines 142-148 — compute_utc_times documented with
       fn compute_utc_times(...) -> impl Future<Output = (Option<String>, Option<String>)>
   actual (backend.rs:284-293): returns (Option<jmap_types::UTCDate>, Option<jmap_types::UTCDate>).
   The UTCDate type was migrated in by commit fb5dbaf (refactor(types,server): migrate calendars and tasks String→UTCDate) — propagation to README missed.

3. README lines 170-178 — get_availability documented with
       utc_start: &str, utc_end: &str
   actual (backend.rs:464-484): &jmap_types::UTCDate. Same fb5dbaf miss.

4. README §'How it works' (lines 196-256) never mentions CallerCtx. Every CalendarsBackend method in the actual trait takes 'caller: &Self::CallerCtx' as first arg after &self (added by commit 514352c). New consumers reading the README will write impls that don't compile, then chase the discrepancy.

5. README line 285 lists a constant JMAP_CALENDARS_PARSE_URI that is not re-exported from this crate today (lib.rs:72 only re-exports JMAP_CALENDARS_URI). The constant likely lives in jmap-calendars-types but consumers cannot import it via the path shown.

The bus-factor cost is concrete: the README is the entry point for any contributor or third-party consumer reading the published crate page. Mismatched signatures make the README adversarial to first-time readers. Workspace README convention (workspace AGENTS.md §README convention) says the six required sections must reflect the actual crate.

Fix: regenerate the trait snippet from src/backend.rs and verify each Future signature inline. Add a 'CallerCtx' note in §'How it works'. Either re-export the parse-URI constant from lib.rs or remove it from the README.
title: README diverges from current trait signatures (UTCDate, PatchObject, CallerCtx)
